title: Software-as-a-Service Subscription Agreement

issues.quote: The term of this agreement (the "Subscription Term") shall be 12 months, beginning on February 1, 2027.
issues.why: No duty; the length of the term is a matter of policy.
issues.fix: The term of this agreement (the "Subscription Term") is 12 months, beginning on February 1, 2027.

issues.anchor: within 30 days of the invoice date
issues.quote: Provider shall invoice the annual fee at the start of each 12-month period, and Customer shall pay each invoice within 30 days of the invoice date.
issues.why: "within 30 days of" could include days before the invoice date.
issues.fix: no later than 30 days after the invoice date

issues.quote: If Customer terminates this agreement under the section titled "Termination for Cause," Provider shall refund any fees paid by Customer for the remainder of the Subscription Term.
Provider shall make its hosted practice-accounting software (the "Service") available to Customer for the Subscription Term, in accordance with the Documentation.
issues.why: "Documentation" is capitalized and used 3 times but never defined. Keyed at the 1st use.
issues.fix: Define "Documentation" (for example, Provider's user guides for the Service as of the date of this agreement).

issues.quote: Provider may, in its sole discretion, modify the Service, except that Provider may not remove any feature that the Documentation describes.
issues.fix: Provider may modify the Service, except that ...

issues.quote: Provider's subcontractors shall comply with the restrictions in this agreement on the use of Customer Data.
issues.why: "shall" with a nonparty subject; the subcontractors are not bound.
issues.fix: Provider shall cause its subcontractors to comply ...

issues.quote: "Customer Data" means all data that Customer or the Customer's personnel enter into the Service.
issues.why: Article before the defined party name (house rule 11); everywhere else the draft correctly says "Customer".

issues.quote: Provider will notify Customer no later than 5 days after Provider discovers any unauthorized access to Customer Data.
Provider represents and warrants that the Service will perform as the Documentation describes.
issues.why: Blake's own draft: statements of fact use "states" (house rule 10).
issues.fix: Provider states that the Service will perform as the Documentation describes.

issues.quote: For the avoidance of doubt, Provider makes no other statement about the Service.
issues.fix: Provider makes no other statement about the Service.

issues.quote: Neither party is liable to the other party for indirect or consequential damages, including without limitation lost profits.
Neither party is liable to the other party for more than $25,000 for claims arising out of this agreement.
issues.why: Unclear whether the $25,000 cap applies to each claim or to all claims in the aggregate.
issues.fix: Neither party is liable to the other party for more than $25,000 in the aggregate for all claims arising out of this agreement.

issues.quote: A notice under this agreement is effective when the recipient receives it by email at the address below the recipient's signature, except that a notice that the recipient receives after 5:00 p.
issues.why: Present tense for a policy about a contingent future event (MSCD 3.334; 3.361 in a matrix clause after a conditional clause; 13.209): the event may never happen, so the verb takes will.
issues.fix: A notice under this agreement will be effective when the recipient receives it by email at the address below the recipient's signature, except that a notice that the recipient receives after 5:00 p

traps.quote: This software-as-a-service subscription agreement is dated January 4, 2027, and is between Ledgerwise Software, Inc., a Tennessee corporation ("Provider"), and Cumberland Valley Dental Group, PLLC, a Tennessee professional limited liability company ("Customer").
traps.why_correct: House exception: "is dated" in the introductory clause.

traps.quote: Customer shall pay Provider an annual subscription fee of $18,000 and a one-time implementation fee of $3,000.
If Customer terminates this agreement under the section titled "Termination for Cause," Provider shall refund any fees paid by Customer for the remainder of the Subscription Term.
traps.why_correct: Cross-reference by heading is the house form (rule 4).

traps.quote: Provider shall return the Customer Data to Customer no later than 30 days after this agreement ends.
traps.why_correct: "Customer Data" is a defined term that is not a party name, so it keeps "the" (house rule 11); compare "the Company Plan".

traps.quote: A notice under this agreement is effective when the recipient receives it by email at the address below the recipient's signature, except that a notice that the recipient receives after 5:00 p.m. Central time is effective on the next day.

notes: Blake's draft.  Formatting is compliant (Aptos 12, left-aligned, bold headings, house enumeration I./A.).  The references to Sections 164.308, 164.310, and 164.312 of Title 45 of the Code of Federal Regulations are regulation references, not internal cross-references.  "Neither party is liable" is correct (no "shall").  About half the issues are subtle: the reduced passive, the undefined Documentation, the nonparty subcontractors, the lone "the Customer's", and the cap scope.

audit.why: Converted from a trap (or added): a notice, payment, change, or transfer is a contingent future event, so MSCD 3.334 (3.361 after a conditional clause; 13.209 for deem; MSCD's own form "A notice ... will be effective if") takes will, not the present tense. Optional pending Blake's answer to question 18 (house rule 8 tense). The passive-voice point stays true: is effective is not passive.
